$comment: Scenarios the differential harness knows about, and what has actually been
captured from real Entra. Schema mirrors azure-apim-emulator's
e2e/differential/testdata/fixture-manifest.json so the family reads the same
way; `capturedAt` and `maxAgeDays` are additions this repo needs because its
fixtures come from a live tenant rather than a recorded service.
status: planned  = named, nothing recorded, harness skips it loudly
captured = a fixture exists and is diffed on every run
A scenario is listed BEFORE it is captured on purpose. The gap between the
planned set and the captured set is the honest measure of how much
differential evidence exists, and deleting the planned rows would make an
empty harness look complete.
`normalizations` is the contract between capture.sh and the harness: capture
folds these to placeholders, the harness is permitted to ignore exactly
these and nothing else. Widening it makes diffs pass — see the mutation
check in the harness, which exists because over-normalising fails silently.
Graph scenarios come in two kinds, because two different things are comparable.
kind=shape records the KEY SET only. The capture tenant holds deliberate
counterparts of the emulator's seed, not copies, so diffing bodies would bury
the protocol differences under content differences that are correct on both
sides. What an emulator must get right is the default projection: which fields
Graph returns when the caller selects none.
kind=error records the whole body, because an error envelope IS protocol.
Graph carries error.code, error.message and an innerError with request ids;
omitting innerError is the classic emulator divergence, and no secret is
returned on any of these paths.

scenarios.what: the app-only token envelope's field set
JWT header + claim names + structural claim values; never the token
wrong client secret — envelope, error_codes, AADSTS number
a grant_type Entra does not implement
a well-formed client_id belonging to no application
the default projection Graph returns for a user when no $select is given
the default projection for a group
the default projection for an application registration
the default projection for a service principal, addressed by appId key
a well-formed object id belonging to nobody: code, message, innerError
a syntactically invalid object id; 400 vs 404 is exactly what a recording settles
$select naming a property the resource does not have
single entity with $select naming a REAL property: does id come back? the emulator now assumes not
collection read with $select: applySelect still retains id here, and that is unwitnessed
does the DEFAULT projection apply to a collection read as it does to a single entity? the emulator now assumes yes
